2 JUDGMENT:
[PER- SHYAM C. CHANDAK, J.] :-
1) Present Applications preferred under Section 482 of the H. C. Shiv APL507.2016.doc Criminal Procedure Code are seeking for quashing of F.I.R. bearing No.02 of 2016, dated 01st January 2016, registered with Park Site Police Station,
Mumbai for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 120-B read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'I.P.C.'), against the Applicants 2) Heard Mrs. Sonal Parab, Mr.Mahesh Devlekar, Ms.Sejal Nagvekar, the learned Advocates for the respective Applicant/s, Mr.Vinod Chate, learned A.P.P. for Respondent-State and Mr.Yogesh Gandhi, learned Advocate for Respondent No.2 in all matters.
Perused the record.

3) The impugned F.I.R. has been filed by the informant Mr.Ketan Kantilal Bhayani wherein he narrated that, he alongwith his brothers Manish Bhayani and Darshak Bhayani are Directors of M/s.Coatings and Coatings (India) Pvt. Ltd. and doing the business of Special Denaturant Spirit (SDS) and wood polish etc.
In February 2015, accused-Ketan Bhat impressed upon the informant that, he is ready to work on commission basis to expand informant's business.
Further, Ketan Bhat informed that, M/s.Gujarat Narmada Valley Fertiliser and Chemical Ltd., Bharuch (for short M/s.Gujarat) and other renowned companies are in need of SDS.

entities.text: Gujarat Narmada Valley Fertiliser and Chemical Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Said SDS is supplied by M/s.Balaji Molasses and Sugar Pvt. Ltd. (for short 'M/s.Balaji'), a H. C. Shiv APL507.2016.doc company owned by accused Prakash Gowda.

entities.text: M/s.Balaji Molasses and Sugar Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Thereafter Ketan Bhat introduced Prakash Gowda to the informant and claimed that, he is associate of Prakash Gowda and suggested the informant to do the business through Prakash Gowda, assuring that it will be helpful.

4) It is alleged that, on 27th February 2015, Ketan Bhat informed the informant that, M/s. Gujarat floated a public tender to purchase SDS and induced the informant to fill the tender giving assurance that, Prakash Gowda will make the SDS available through his company M/s.Balaji.
Thereafter, during telephonic talk arranged by Ketan Bhat, Prakash Gowda assured the informant to supply the SDS at Rs.26.75 per litre through his company.
Hence, on 14 th March 2015, the informant submitted the tender to supply the requisite 15 lacs litres of SDS and deposited Rs.10 lacs.

The tender submitted by informant was accepted on 3rd April 2015, subject to supplying the goods till 31st May 2015.
5)
It is alleged that, in April 2015, Ketan Bhat arranged a meeting of informant with Prakash Gowda and his associates namely Applicants-Amar Sona and Nijal Shah.
During the said meeting Prakash Gowda assured that, he will supply the 15 lacs litres of SDS at Rs.26.75 inclusive of taxes before 31 st May 2015.
At that time, Applicants-Amar Sona and Nijal Shah assured the informant that, H. C.
Shiv APL507.2016.doc
the business conduct of Prakash Gowda is clean, good and there is no harm in carrying business with him

. Accordingly, on 18 th April 2015, an agreement was entered into Nijal Navin Shah vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120855721/
3 between the company of the informant and M/s.Balaji.

sentences.text: The terms and conditions thereof were also entered into the agreement.

At that time Prakash Gowda issued certain undated cheques to win the confidence of informant.
6) It is alleged that, thereafter as instructed by Prakash Gowda, the informant paid Rs.2 crores on 21 st April 2015, by a cheque and Rs.2,01,25,000/- on 5th May 2015, by RTGS in the bank account of M/s.Balaji.

However, later on accused-Prakash Gowda told the informant that, instead of M/s.Balaji he would supply the SDS through M/s.John Distilleries Pvt. Ltd., Chitali, District Ahmednagar (for short, 'M/s.John'), of which he is a Director.

Accordingly, Prakash Gowda sent the Delivery Orders dated 25 th April 2015 and 30th April 2015 for 3 lacs litres and 12 lacs litres of SDS respectively,
issued by M/s.John, through M/s.Vaarini Ethanol.
In turn, the informant supplied to M/s.John the necessary chemicals to be mixed in the SDS to be supplied.
Thereafter, the sample of the said mixture was approved by the concerned lab.
7) It is alleged that, on 28th May 2015, the informant sent his truck to M/s.John to collect the goods under the agreement.
H. C. Shiv APL507.2016.doc
However, the delivery was declined.

On enquiry with Mr.Jayaraj,
Factory Manager of M/s.John, he told that without licence issued by the concerned Excise Department, the goods cannot be delivered.
Hence, the informant contacted Prakash Gowda and Ketan Bhat and told that no such licence is required.
Meanwhile, the tender compliance date 31st May, 2015 was over and the subsequent talk with M/s.John was fruitless.
Thereafter, the informant tried to contact Prakash Gowda and Ketan Bhat but they were not found.
The talk with the Officer of State Excise, Ahmednagar did not help the situation.

Meanwhile M/s.Gujarat put the informant on legal notice that, if the 15 lacs litres SDS is not supplied they would procure that goods from other companies and recover the damages thereof from the informant.
Thereafter, the informant had a meeting with Prakash Gowda, Ketan Bhat, Applicants-Amar Sona and Nijal Shah.

However, Prakash Gowda and Ketan Bhat told that, the said agreement with informant's company has been over and if the informant wants the goods, he should enter into a new agreement as per the current market rate and canceled the cheques issued as security against the advance payment of Rs.4,01,25,000/- by the informant.
8) It is alleged that thereafter informant and his Manager- H. C. Shiv APL507.2016.doc Kaushik Parekh met with Ketan Bhat and Mr.Limbachia, office bearer of M/s.Gujarat, on 10th June, 2015.

At that time Ketan Bhat told the informant that, Prakash Gowda is well acquainted with M/s.Gujarat and he may help in extending the time to supply the SDS to M/s.Gujarat and suggested to obtain the goods from M/s.John.
Therefore, again the informant met with Mr.Jayaraj on 19 th June, 2015.
However, the informant was told that, there is no direct agreement of the informant's company with M/s.John and nor the price of subject goods was received by M/s.John.
Thereafter.
Prakash Gowda and Ketan Bhat could not be contacted.

Thus, the Applicants, Ketan Bhat, Prakash Gowda, Mr.Jayaraj, Distillery Manage - Mr.Dhotre and clerk Mr.Mane of M/s.John cheated the informant and misappropriated the price of subject SDS to be supplied.

Thereafter, Applicant-Amar Sona threaten Manish Bhayani on a phone call that, if they Nijal Navin Shah vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120855721/
4 dare to go to the Court they won't get their money atleast for 10 years etc.

sentences.text: Hence, police registered the impugned F.I.R. against the Applicants, Prakash Gowda and others.

9) Learned Advocate Ms.Sonal Parab for Applicant Nijal Shah submitted that, through common acquaintance this Applicant was introduced with Prakash Gowda in the year 2015 in respect of the development work of the latter's properties at Bangalore.
On the H. C. Shiv APL507.2016.doc request of Prakash Gowda, the Applicant attended the said meeting held in April 2015 in relation to the complained transaction.
Therefore, the Applicant was completely unaware of the deal and the transaction in question.
The Applicant signed the said agreement but only as a witness at the instance of informant and his brother Manish Bhayani, as there was no witness from the side of Prakash Gowda.
The Applicant was never a business associate of Prakash Gowda.
Thus, the Applicant is innocent, however, he has been falsely implicated in this case.
10) Learned Advocate Mr.Mahesh Devlekar for Applicants- Mr.Jayaraj, Mr.Dhotre and Mr.Mane submitted that, the Applicants were working with M/s.John.
He submitted that, the relevant chemical sample report, issued by Hawkins Institute, was submitted late by the informant.
The informant did not obtain necessary import permit.
Thus, he failed to comply with the Consent Letters issued by M/s. John to supply the goods.
Therefore, the Order to supply the subject SDS placed by Prakash Gowda was cancelled by M/s.John and substantial advance amount was transferred to M/s.Balaji.
The Applicants are third party to the subject transaction.
Therefore, the Applicants are innocent.

11) Learned Advocate Ms.Sejal Nagvekar, for Applicant- H. C. Shiv APL507.2016.doc Amar Sona submitted that, this Applicant has not played any role in this crime except introducing Applicant-Nijal Shah to Prakash Gowda for the latter's buildings'
development work.
The Applicant is not beneficiary of the said offence.
As such, the Applicant is innocent.
Lastly, that the dispute is of civil nature.
12) Learned A.P.P. submitted that, there is sufficient material against the Applicants showing their involvement in this crime as they committed it in connivance with main accused-Prakash Gowda.

Learned Advocate Mr. Yogesh Gandhi for Respondent No.2 supported the submissions made by learned A.P.P. He submitted that, the facts narrated in the FIR clearly disclose the commission of alleged crime by the Applicants.
That, there are no merits in the Applications and therefore it may be dismissed.
13) In support of his submissions, the learned A.P.P. submitted a report produced by the Investigating Officer.

This report clearly shows that, immediately after deposit of Rs.2 crores with M/s.Balaji by the informant, Prakash Gowda paid Rs.25 lacs to Applicant-Amar Sona in two parts i.e. Rs.10 lacs on 24/04/2015 and Rs.15 lacs on 11/06/2015.
In so far Applicant-Nijal Shah is concerned, he has received Rs.10 lacs on 23/04/2015 from Prakash Gowda through a banking transaction.
Both the Applicants failed to H. C. Shiv APL507.2016.doc give a satisfactory reason behind accepting the money as above.

Despite Applicant-Amar Sona knew that, crimes of fraud were registered against Prakash Gowda in Karnataka, Applicant-Amar Sona and Nijal Shah convinced the Nijal Navin Shah vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120855721/
5 informant that, Prakash Gowda's business conduct is transparent and good and signed on the agreement.

entities.text: Nijal Navin Shah vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, both these Applicants helped to commit this offence by causing the informant to trust on Prakash Gowda.

14) In so far as the Applicants in Criminal Application No.1284 of 2016 are concerned, the report of police clearly indicates that, even though M/s.John did not comply the order to supply 15 lacs liters of SDS, they helped in returning Rs.90 lacs part of the advanced amount, in the bank account of M/s.Vaarini Ethanol of Prakash Gowda instead of M/s.Balaji through whose account the advance Rs.1 crore were received.
Thus, these Applicants helped to misappropriate the advance amount paid by the informant.
15) In view thereof, in our considered opinion, there is prima facie case of offences alleged against the Applicants.
In so far as the story put forth by the Applicants is concerned, it constitute their defence which they will have to establish in the trial.
Hence, veracity of their story cannot be examined by this Court as it would be a mini trial, which is not permissible.
It is by now the settled H. C. Shiv APL507.2016.doc position of law that, this Court cannot conduct a mini trial under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. while considering an Application for quashing of F.I.R.
As such all the Applications have no merits and are liable to be dismissed.
16) Applications are accordingly dismissed.
(SHYAM C. CHANDAK,J.) (A. S. GADKARI  PREETI  HEERO
JAYANI
